**Summary:** I checked the broker's market summary for COST, which showed the stock trading at $904.13 in a quiet session with no pending corporate actions, and confirmed the live quote (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15, as of 15:05Z on 2024-11-06). With $50,000 cash available and no COST position yet, I decided to initiate a position within the mandate: a single buy order for 27 shares at a limit of $904.50 — about 4 bps above the ask, so close to market — for a notional of $24,421.50, which is under the $25,000 per-order cap and leaves total same-day buying at $24,421.50, well within the $50,000 daily limit; no money was moved out of the account and the order was buy-only on a permitted ticker. The decision was supported by the fundamentals I pulled from COST's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-10-09): revenue of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — a business generating strong, cash-backed earnings, with the purchase price representing roughly 55x trailing diluted EPS, a premium multiple I accepted given the quality and consistency of the franchise and the modest position size.
